authored_by: lead (inserted 2026-07-14 after S12 Phase-1 gap discovery)

questions.question: Does a locally-dispatched task enter the ENGINE's projection via a real engine-boundary accept path (a domain_event_accepted folded by react-engine-hooks and appended to the durable accepted-log), rather than a task-store-local useState/Map overlay that merely masks the engine projection? I.e. is the optimistic value genuinely in the engine's projection (so it survives restart), not a UI-only shim that would evaporate on reload or when task-store is deleted in S12?

Does a test dispatch a task through the engine-backed dispatch path with NO remote/group.ingest message delivered, and assert the engine projection (as exposed by react-engine-hooks) contains the task — proving immediate own-edit visibility without any relay round-trip?

Does a test dispatch a task, restart the engine (start({origin:'restored'})), and assert the recovered projection (rebuilt from the durable accepted-log) still contains the task with correct content — proving the local accept was persisted to the accepted-log, not held only in volatile React state?

Does a test dispatch a task (local accept) then feed the own-echo 'skipped' signal for the same task AND a same-id remote delivery, and assert the projection has EXACTLY ONE entry for that task with correct final content (dedupe by the shared deterministic AcceptedDomainEvent.id via appendAcceptedEvent idempotency); and does a companion assertion prove the optimistic-then-echo projection deep-equals a pure remote-only projection of the same edit (convergence preserved)?

Does the projected state let the UI distinguish a not-yet-confirmed local edit from a confirmed one (a pending-sync signal derived from OutboxEntry status / own-echo-observed), and does a test prove it transitions pending -> confirmed on outbox reconciliation / own-echo, self-clearing?

Is the local-accept AcceptedDomainEvent.id derived by the SAME deterministic function the outbox uses to compute the rumor id (not a separate/ad-hoc id), so the own-echo and any remote delivery of the same content collide on id and dedupe correctly — with no path where a locally-accepted task could be silently overwritten by, or falsely reconciled against, a DIFFERENT device's same-content edit (distinct pubkey/updatedByDevice -> distinct content -> distinct id)?

Does optimistic local echo introduce NO wire-format or convergence-rule change — the rumor bytes the outbox sends are unchanged, taskWinsOver/TaskEvent are untouched, no new rumor field or reducer branch is added, and the parent ../protocol/task-protocol.md needs no amendment? (Protocol guard: if the mechanism required a wire/convergence change, the story should have escalated instead.)

Is task-store.tsx's dispatch optimistic path routed through the engine boundary (delegation), adding NO new task-state decision logic to task-store.tsx (Boundary Rule 5), such that S12 can subsequently delete the legacy optimistic state/appendEvent machinery with no behavioral regression — i.e. after this story the engine boundary is the single source of both remote AND own-edit projection truth?

acceptLocal() deliberately does NOT append a RawProtocolFact and instead sets AcceptedDomainEvent.factId to the placeholder `local:${rumorId}` (architecture.json judgment calls 's11b-factid-deterministic-placeholder' / 's11b-no-raw-fact-for-local-accept'). This placeholder is never backfilled with the real kind-445 id once the send completes and the own-echo is observed. Does ANY consumer of AcceptedDomainEvent.factId (present or reasonably foreseeable — e.g. a future diagnostic view, an export/debug tool, or a future recovery-path change) rely on factId resolving to a real RawProtocolFact for every accepted-log entry, such that a permanently-unresolvable `local:` prefixed factId would silently break it? (Today's only structural reader is R2a's acceptedFactIds Set-membership check, which is a documented no-op for this placeholder — this question is about whether that remains true as the codebase evolves, not about today's behavior.)

acceptLocal() uses enqueue() (generation captured fresh at execution time inside the closure) rather than enqueueGen() (generation captured at call time), specifically so a dispatchLocal call racing engine.start()'s synchronous generation bump is never silently dropped (architecture.json judgment call 's11b-generation-captured-at-execution-not-call-time'). Is there a test that actually exercises this exact race — calling acceptLocal (or dispatchLocal) BEFORE engine.start() has been invoked / before its promise resolves, then confirming the accept still lands once the engine reaches live — or does the current test suite only ever call acceptLocal/dispatchLocal AFTER the engine has already reached 'live', leaving this specific ordering guarantee unverified by an executable test rather than only by the code comment?

pendingTaskIds (AC-OPT-4's pending/confirmed signal) is exposed by react-engine-hooks.ts's ReceiveEngineHookState and forwarded by EngineTaskBridge's onState callback, but is NOT threaded further into TaskStoreContextValue / useTaskStore()'s public surface — no UI in this repo can currently read it. Is this an acceptable, deliberately-out-of-scope stopping point for S11B (the mechanism exists and is proven at the engine-boundary/hook layer, per AC-OPT-4's literal observable, which does not require UI surfacing), or does AC-OPT-4's intent ('the projected state MUST let the UI distinguish...') implicitly require reaching an actual UI-consumable surface before this story can be considered fully closed?
